properties.name: Merneptah Stele (Israel Stele)
properties.surveyor_caveat: Stele is real Late Bronze Egyptian victory text naming 'Israel'. Findspot is Merneptah’s Theban mortuary temple area; object lives in Cairo. Do not overclaim every campaign geography from the poetic list. PoliceBot: egyptianmuseumcairo.eg CAUTION — prefer egymonuments.gov.eg once cleared.
properties.support: Granite victory stele of Pharaoh Merneptah; includes the earliest widely accepted extra-biblical reference to Israel as a people in Canaan.
properties.sources: Cairo Museum collection; Merneptah mortuary temple find context; DigIntoScripture MER-01

properties.name: Tel Dan Stele (House of David)
properties.surveyor_caveat: Aramaic victory inscription; 'House of David' reading is the mainstream scholarly consensus with ongoing fringe debate — keep Linguist-safe wording if Gospel copy cites the phrase. Fragments found at Tel Dan; displayed at Israel Museum (site may show replica/context).
properties.support: 9th-century BCE Aramaic stele fragments from Tel Dan that refer to the 'House of David' — key extra-biblical Judah/Davidic dynasty witness.
properties.sources: Israel Museum / IAA; Tel Dan excavations; DigIntoScripture DAN-STELE / DAN-01

properties.name: Ketef Hinnom silver amulets (priestly blessing)
properties.surveyor_caveat: Tiny rolled silver scrolls with text close to Numbers 6 priestly blessing; paleographic dating has scholarly range (often late Iron Age). Present as early biblical-text witnesses, not as 'the original Torah scroll.'
properties.support: Two silver amulets from a Jerusalem burial repository preserving an early form of the priestly blessing.
properties.sources: Israel Museum; Ketef Hinnom excavations; DigIntoScripture KET-01

properties.name: Siloam Tunnel Inscription
properties.found_at_name: Jerusalem – City of David / Gihon (Hezekiah’s Tunnel tradition)
properties.surveyor_caveat: Hebrew inscription describing the tunnel breakthrough; removed in the Ottoman period and now in Istanbul. Replica/context at City of David / tunnel visitor area. Tunnel=Hezekiah tradition is strong historically; keep Discover-careful wording on engineering phases.
properties.support: Hebrew rock inscription from the Siloam / Hezekiah’s Tunnel water system describing how two crews met.
properties.sources: Istanbul Archaeology Museums; City of David / Gihon water system; DigIntoScripture COD-03 / JER-NT-01

properties.name: Magdala Stone
properties.surveyor_caveat: First-century synagogue stone with Temple imagery; displayed at Magdala. Ministry/pilgrimage packaging on site — archaeology is real; keep Gospel Mary Magdalene hometown as tradition packaging separate from the stone’s Temple motifs.
properties.support: Carved stone from Magdala’s first-century synagogue showing menorah / Temple-related imagery.

properties.name: Mesha Stele (Moabite Stone)
properties.surveyor_caveat: Moabite victory inscription of King Mesha mentioning Omri/Israel and YHWH; 19th-century find history is messy (squeeze/reconstruction). Object in Louvre. Do not treat every line of historical geography as settled without caveats.
properties.support: Basalt stele of Moab’s King Mesha reporting conflict with Israel — major extra-biblical Iron Age witness naming YHWH.
properties.sources: Louvre; Dhiban / Dibon context; DigIntoScripture DIB-01

properties.name: Cyrus Cylinder
properties.surveyor_caveat: Achaemenid royal inscription on Persian policy toward subject peoples/temples. Useful backdrop for Ezra/return themes; do not claim the cylinder quotes Ezra verbatim.
properties.support: Clay cylinder of Cyrus the Great from Babylon describing restoration policies after conquering Babylon.

properties.name: Dead Sea Scrolls (Qumran corpus — museum display)
properties.displayed_at_museum: Israel Museum — Shrine of the Book
properties.surveyor_caveat: Scrolls are a manuscript corpus, not one object. Find context = Judean Desert caves near Qumran; major displays at Shrine of the Book. Keep Holy Bible as canon; scrolls illuminate Second Temple textual world. Also attach QUM-NT-01 as same complex.
properties.support: Second Temple Jewish manuscripts from the Judean Desert caves, including biblical books centuries older than medieval codices.
properties.sources: Israel Museum Shrine of the Book; Qumran / Judean Desert finds; DigIntoScripture QUM-01 / QUM-NT-01

properties.name: Pilate Stone (Pontius Pilate inscription)
properties.surveyor_caveat: Latin dedicatory inscription naming Pontius Pilate, prefect of Judea (IAA 1961-529). Found reused in Caesarea’s theater; original in Israel Museum; replica often on-site. Does not narrate the Gospel trial — it confirms Pilate’s historical office/title.
properties.support: Only widely accepted contemporary inscription naming Pontius Pilate as prefect of Judea.
properties.sources: Israel Museum / IAA 1961-529; Caesarea Maritima excavations; DigIntoScripture CAES-01,CAES-02

properties.name: Lachish Reliefs (Sennacherib’s siege of Lachish)
properties.found_at_name: Nineveh (SW Palace) — reliefs found here; scene depicts Lachish
properties.surveyor_caveat: SPECIAL LINK: carved at Nineveh, depicting the Assyrian siege of Lachish (not found at Tel Lachish). Pair museum pin with BOTH NIN-01 (findspot of panels) and LAC-01 (depicted city). Do not say the slabs were dug at Lachish.
properties.support: Assyrian palace wall reliefs showing Sennacherib’s capture of Lachish — visual match to the 701 BCE Judah campaign.
properties.sources: British Museum Assyrian galleries; Nineveh SW Palace; DigIntoScripture NIN-01 + LAC-01

properties.name: Horned altar from Beersheba
properties.surveyor_caveat: Dismantled horned altar stones reused in storehouse walls at Tel Beersheba; reconstructed for display. Speaks to cult practice / reform debates — do not force a single sermon point beyond the archaeology.
properties.support: Reassembled four-horned ashlar altar from Tel Beersheba, a major Judahite southern administrative center.
properties.sources: Israel Museum; Tel Beersheba excavations; DigIntoScripture BEE-01
